name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Kelly retiring but seat held by Democrats
Republican candidate has raised essentially nothing
model.rationale: This is a heavily Democratic open seat where Donna Miller has raised $2.4 million plus $4.5 million in outside support, while Michael Noack shows no meaningful fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win at 96%, and fundamentals point to a roughly 24-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise would require a major scandal or a collapse in Democratic turnout in this Chicago-area district.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
IL-02 is a heavily Democratic Chicago-area district that Robin Kelly is leaving to run for Senate. Donna Miller enters as the clear favorite, backed by $2.4 million in fundraising and roughly $4.5 million in outside support, while Republican Michael Noack shows no reported fundraising or outside spending. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent.

The district's D+18 partisan lean and the absence of any competitive polling or expert ratings pointing the other way make this a Safe Democratic seat. The main uncertainty is the open-seat dynamic, which adds modest risk but is unlikely to change the outcome.
